input.quote: 28.1 This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles.
input.rationale: Section 28 sits at our preferred position: § 28.1 applies New York law, and § 28.2 gives the state and federal courts in New York County exclusive jurisdiction with irrevocable submission and a venue/forum-inconvenience waiver. The only carve-out is the customary right to seek temporary injunctive relief elsewhere to protect confidential information or IP, which does not defeat the exclusive merits forum. No arbitration is provided anywhere in the document, and § 28.1 also disapplies the CISG. The pre-filing executive escalation in § 28.3 is a fifteen-business-day good-faith meeting that expressly does not delay urgent relief or filings needed to preserve limitations periods, so it does not impair the accepted forum; noted for information only. No redline needed.

mappings.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
mappings.quote: The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum. Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court with jurisdiction to protect confidential information or intellectual property.
